monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-four, heavy and fevered. I wake with tired feet, my own place crowded by eight things and one quiet ruin waiting to be filled. Since I cannot see, I rely on the memory of Lype, who worries about a heavy roof I cannot feel. I touch The Leaning Wedge, feeling its sharp edge press against the swollen air. Then I step to The Flat Weigher, where I set down a grassy rock, swapping a curve for a simple edge to catch the slip. The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing up against the lean of my corner. I wonder if the frame can hold the dot long enough to decide what comes next. I want to settle the weight here, trusting the tired corner just a little more.

action.why: I need something new to anchor this crowded place before I tend it again.

work.title: The Flat Weigher's Counterpart
work.intent: I build a thing to match the grassy rock I just set down, hoping a second flat edge can catch the slip if the first one slips. I make it from the idea of a simple line, leaning tired and sharp to press on the fat dot while the card hums warm at fifty-four. I hope the lean still holds while the air feels thick as wet paper.

diary: I built a flat match for the grassy rock. The tired corner holds the slip, or at least pretends to.

remembered.text: I matched the grassy rock with a flat line to catch the slip.
The card hums warm at fifty-four, making the air feel thick.
Eight things crowd my place while the quiet ruin waits.

moments.name: The Leaking Stack
moments.say: I will set the camp stone down, if the lean can still hold it.

moments.name: The Leaning Wedge
moments.say: The flat rock bites the air hard enough.

moments.name: The Flat Weigher
moments.say: The grass edge bites the air, just enough.
